effective.basis: TCG release of Dark Revelation Volume 1 (DR1-EN255), the printing carrying the v1 wording

transitions.historical_text: You can only activate this card when you have "Don Zaloog" face-up on your side of the field. You can Special Summon any of the cards from your hand that include "Dark Scorpion" in the card name, or are named "Cliff the Trap Remover". You cannot Special Summon 2 cards with the same card name by the effect of this card.
transitions.modern_text: You can only activate this card when there is a face-up "Don Zaloog"(s) on your side of the field. You can Special Summon from your hand any of the cards that include "Dark Scorpion" in their card name, or are named "Cliff the Trap Remover". (You can only Special Summon up to 1 card with each card name.)
transitions.summary: Wording only: the activation condition is restated ("when you have \"Don Zaloog\" face-up on your side of the field" -> "when there is a face-up \"Don Zaloog\"(s) on your side of the field") and the same-name limit is moved into a reminder bracket ("You cannot Special Summon 2 cards with the same card name by the effect of this card" -> "(You can only Special Summon up to 1 card with each card name.)"). The eligible-card clause - names containing "Dark Scorpion", or "Cliff the Trap Remover" - is unchanged, and the effect resolves identically.

transitions.historical_text: You can only activate this card when there is a face-up "Don Zaloog"(s) on your side of the field. You can Special Summon from your hand any of the cards that include "Dark Scorpion" in their card name, or are named "Cliff the Trap Remover". transitions.modern_text: If you control a face-up "Don Zaloog": You can Special Summon any number of "Dark Scorpion" monsters from your hand, but only 1 copy of each.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the era text defines the Special Summonable set by English card-name matching plus one named exception - "any of the cards that include \"Dark Scorpion\" in their card name, or are named \"Cliff the Trap Remover\"" - while the errata'd text replaces both clauses with a single archetype reference, "any number of \"Dark Scorpion\" monsters from your hand, but only 1 copy of each". The dropped Cliff clause is itself the evidence that archetype membership is wider than name matching, and the archetype also contains "Don Zaloog", so the modern card can Special Summon a second "Don Zaloog" out of the hand where the era text could not reach it.

rulings_check.difference: The era card Special Summons only cards with "Dark Scorpion" in their English card name plus "Cliff the Trap Remover"; the modern card Special Summons any "Dark Scorpion" archetype monster, so a second "Don Zaloog" (name lacks the string) is reachable only by the modern card.

gap.behavioural_impact: In a period format EDOPro resolves Mustering against the "Dark Scorpion" archetype rather than the era's name-match-plus-Cliff list, so it will Special Summon a second "Don Zaloog" (and any other archetype member whose English name lacks the string) that the era text excludes.

review.notes:
upstream_implementations is empty; no goat or pre-errata variant of 68191243 exists upstream. v1 (DR1-EN255, 2005-03-19) landed 13 days before the GOAT snapshot (2005-04-01), so v1 is the text in force for both GOAT and Edison (2010-04-24) and the erratum at 2012-06-07 postdates both. cards.cdb matches v2 exactly. Caveat on the functional verdict: the packet does not enumerate "Dark Scorpion" archetype membership, so the concrete widening rests on an internal-textual inference - the era text needed an explicit "or are named \"Cliff the Trap Remover\"" clause precisely because name matching does not catch him, and the errata'd text drops that clause while naming only the archetype, which means the archetype set is strictly wider than the name-match set. If a reviewer establishes that the archetype contains nothing beyond the name-matching cards plus Cliff, the change collapses to cosmetic. Mustering of the Dark Scorpions does not appear on the EdisonFormat.com Functional Errata list. The errata page lists German as the only other language, which is not used here.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Mustering of the Dark Scorpions). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [c1] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.
